rules.title: Prohibition on Using or Distributing Common Pricing Algorithms to Collude or Coerce
rules.quote: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade. Separately, businesses are also prohibited from using or offering common pricing algorithms if they coerce users to adopt the algorithm's recommendations on pricing or other commercial terms within California for the same or similar products or services.
rules.summary: Businesses cannot use or distribute common pricing algorithms (technology with two or more users that uses competitor information) to collude on pricing or to coerce users to adopt algorithmic pricing recommendations.
rules.effective_date_evidence: As of January 1, 2026, businesses are subject to the Cartwright Act's latest amendments, including an express prohibition on certain usages of pricing algorithms.
rules.exemption_note: Single-firm algorithms using only a business's own data are not covered by the law.
rules.penalty: Criminal fines: up to $6 million for corporations or twice the gain or loss, up to $1 million for individuals or twice the gain or loss. Civil fines: up to $1 million based on statutory factors including nature, seriousness, duration, and willfulness of conduct.
